title: Python fundamentals
summary: Think in small steps: take an input, transform it, and show a result.
points: Python uses indentation to group statements. Use four spaces per indentation level consistently.
Names and strings are case-sensitive. # begins a comment outside a string.
print displays values, separating multiple arguments with spaces by default. input always returns a string.
Parentheses make precedence explicit: multiplication happens before addition. / is true division; // is floor division; % gives a remainder; ** is exponentiation.
code:
minutes = 30
watch = 18
remaining = minutes - watch
print("Time left:", remaining)
mistake: Do not assume user input is already a number. Convert and validate it.
challenge: Ask for a daily budget and print how many minutes remain after a 12-minute lesson.

diagram.caption: A program transforms information through explicit steps.

title: Variables & data types
summary: A name refers to an object. The object has a type; the name can later refer to another object.
points: Use int("5") to convert numeric text before arithmetic. Invalid numeric text raises ValueError.
String indexes start at 0; -1 selects the last character. A slice includes its start and excludes its stop.
len reports a sequence’s length. Multiplying a string repeats it. An f-string evaluates expressions inside braces.
Empty strings and zero are false in boolean contexts. Nonempty strings, including "False", are truthy. None represents the absence of a value.
mistake: "5" + "2" produces "52". It does not perform numeric addition.
challenge: Extract the first three characters of your name, then print them with your age using an f-string.

diagram.title: Variables & data types at a glance
diagram.caption: A variable name points to a value; operations depend on that value’s type.

title: Control flow
summary: Decisions choose a branch; loops repeat a useful step.
points: if / elif / else executes the first matching branch. Use == to compare; = assigns.
for visits items in an iterable. range(start, stop, step) stops before stop and defaults to start 0 and step 1.
while repeats while its condition is truthy. Change state so a loop can finish.
break exits the nearest loop. continue skips to its next iteration. pass is a no-operation placeholder.
and, or, and not combine or negate truth values. Expressions can short-circuit.
code:
total = 0
for number in range(1, 4):
    total += number
print(total)
mistake: An unchanged while condition can produce an infinite loop.
challenge: Print the even numbers from 2 through 10 using range.

diagram.title: Control flow at a glance
diagram.caption: Only the matching branch runs; execution then continues after the block.

title: Functions
summary: Give a reusable piece of behavior a name, inputs, and a clear result.
points: def defines a function. Parameters name its inputs; arguments supply values when it is called.
return ends the current call and gives a result to the caller. No explicit result means None; printing is not returning.
Default arguments are evaluated once when the function is defined. Use None and create a fresh list inside instead of a mutable list default.
Keyword arguments bind by name. *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple; **kwargs collects extra named arguments into a dictionary.
Assignment inside a function normally creates a local name. It does not reassign a same-named global variable unless explicitly declared global.
mistake: A function that prints a result but does not return it gives the caller None.
challenge: Write a function that takes a price and discount and returns the discounted price.

diagram.title: Functions at a glance
diagram.caption: Separate the calculation from the code that displays its result.

title: Data structures
summary: Choose a collection by how you need to access and change the information.
points: Lists preserve order and are mutable. append adds an item; list.copy makes a shallow copy. Nested mutable values can still be shared.
Tuples are immutable sequences. A single-item tuple needs a comma: (5,).
Sets contain unique hashable elements; do not rely on iteration order. Dictionaries map unique keys to values.
d[key] raises KeyError for a missing key. d.get(key, default) supplies a fallback.
Comprehensions build collections from iterables. sorted returns a new list; list.sort mutates a list and returns None.
Assigning b = a does not copy a list. Both names refer to the same object.
code:
scores = [3, 1, 3]
print(sorted(set(scores)))
squares = [n * n for n in [1, 2, 3]]
print(squares)
mistake: Changing an aliased list changes the object seen through both names.
challenge: Build a dictionary of three learner names and scores; safely read a missing learner with a default.

diagram.title: Data structures at a glance
diagram.caption: A good collection choice makes the next operation simple.

title: Object-oriented programming
summary: A class groups behavior with the state that behavior operates on.
points: class defines a class; calling it normally creates an instance. __init__ initializes instance state.
self is the conventional name for the current instance in instance methods. Store instance attributes as self.name.
Class attributes are available through the class and its instances. Instance attributes may shadow them; shared mutable class attributes need care.
class Dog(Animal): declares inheritance. A subclass can override an inherited method.
isinstance also recognizes subclasses. super supports cooperative calls through the method resolution order.
mistake: Putting a mutable list on the class can unintentionally share it between instances.
challenge: Create a Learner class with a name and a method that returns a greeting.

rows: Function accessed through an object or class
Replace inherited behavior in a subclass

diagram.title: Object-oriented programming at a glance
diagram.caption: Each instance can carry its own state while sharing behavior defined on the class.

title: File handling
summary: Files keep information beyond a single program run. Choose modes carefully.
points: with open(...) as f manages closing the file when the block exits, including when an exception is raised.
r reads; w writes and truncates existing content; a appends; rb reads bytes. Use an explicit encoding such as utf-8 for text.
read reads remaining content; readline reads one line and retains a newline if present. Iterating over a file processes lines without reading all of it at once.
seek(0) returns the file position to the beginning. Reads happen from the current position.
json.dump writes JSON to a file-like object; json.load reads JSON from one. dumps and loads work with strings.
code:
from io import StringIO
with StringIO("Python\nPractice\n") as file:
    print(file.readline().strip())
    print(file.readline().strip())
mistake: Opening a valuable existing file with w erases its old content. The example uses an in-memory file safely.
challenge: In a disposable folder, write a short note, then reopen it with r and print it.

diagram.title: File handling at a glance
diagram.caption: The with block makes the cleanup step explicit and dependable.

title: Exception handling
summary: Handle the failures you expect and let unexpected problems remain visible.
points: Put a risky operation in try and handle a specific exception in except. ValueError often signals an invalid conversion; ZeroDivisionError signals division by zero.
Use except ValueError as err to inspect the exception. Avoid bare except when you only intend to catch one kind of error.
else runs when the try suite finishes normally. finally provides cleanup during normal control flow, whether or not an exception was raised; it cannot protect against forceful process termination.
raise ValueError("message") explicitly signals invalid input. Clear error messages help the caller recover.
output:
Enter a whole number
Attempt finished
mistake: Catching every exception and ignoring it can hide real defects.
challenge: Convert a text input to an integer and show a helpful message if conversion fails.

diagram.title: Exception handling at a glance
diagram.caption: Recovery should be specific to the failure you actually understand.

title: Modules & packages
summary: Split code into reusable files and isolate project dependencies.
points: A .py file can be a module. import math binds the module; math.sqrt accesses a member. import math as m introduces an alias.
from math import pi binds the selected name directly. Avoid wildcard imports when they obscure where names originate.
__name__ equals "__main__" when a file is run as the main program. Use the guard to separate entry-point behavior from import behavior.
pip installs packages. python -m pip runs pip with the chosen interpreter; virtual environments keep project packages separate.
A local file named json.py or math.py can shadow the library you intended to import.
code:
import math as m
print(m.sqrt(9))
from math import pi
print(round(pi, 2))
mistake: Installing into one Python environment and running another can cause confusing import errors.
challenge: Create a helper module with one function and import it from a second file.

diagram.title: Modules & packages at a glance
diagram.caption: Imports connect small, focused modules into a program.

title: Working with APIs
summary: An API request crosses a network boundary. Plan for missing data and failures.
points: An endpoint is a URL exposing an operation or resource. GET normally retrieves a representation; POST commonly submits data for processing or creation.
Check status and response structure before using the result. 404 means Not Found; 429 indicates too many requests.
Set timeouts, handle connection errors, and respect retry guidance. A response arriving does not mean the operation succeeded.
JSON text is not a Python object. json.loads decodes text; JSON true becomes True and null becomes None. json.dumps encodes an object to JSON text.
Keep private API credentials in server-side secret configuration. Do not put them in public repositories or browser code.
code:
import json
response_text = '{"count": 2, "ok": true}'
data = json.loads(response_text)
if data.get("ok") is True:
    print(data["count"])
mistake: Do not call every response a success or assume every body has the fields you expect. This example decodes a sample response without making a network call.
challenge: Decode a sample JSON response and handle a missing field with a useful fallback.

diagram.title: Working with APIs at a glance
diagram.caption: Network failures, status errors, and malformed data need separate handling.
